messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — overnight perf CI showed a p99 spike on the small-batch nightly run. CI alert (run-1234) at 00:12. Anyone pick this up?
ci-bot: ALERT: perf-ci/nightly-smallbatch run-1234 p99 latency +72% vs baseline. link: https://ci.internal/runs/1234 :rotating_light:
Kevin L: saw this. repro locally on the runner image (r-2026-03). p95 up too, but p99 is worse. I can profile if you point me to the trace id.
Sasha R: @Kevin L I kicked off heap+cpu profiling job against that run: https://prof.internal/jobs/998 — collecting kernels+perf. will take ~20m :hourglass:
Maria G: trace id is trace-2500-abc. repro command: ```./bench_runner --model gpt-small --batch 2 --seq 512 --reps 100 --trace trace-2500-abc``` Add --debug-sched to get scheduler traces.
Leo: curious if this is the same regression after the allocator tweak (commit 9f7b2a). I can try a patch that pins old allocator and run a smoke benchmark tonight.
Tanvi: I can start a canary with quantization off and the old kernel selector. Tagging @Sasha R to share profiler when ready.
Kevin L: quick check: are we seeing increased tail due to batching? logs show a few 3s stalls at startup: ```[worker0] stall: flush_cache took 3012ms``` might be warmup-related.
Sasha R: profiler uploaded: https://prof.internal/reports/998 — main hotspot is vk_mem_alloc and thread wake latency. Attaching flame: (short) looks like scheduler wake is ~2.8ms per event.
Maria G: ok plan: Sasha will finish profile and share artifacts. Leo + Kevin will run pinned-allocator canary. Tanvi will start canary with q=off and old-kernel. I'll open a tracking issue and assign bisect if needed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin L: ping if you want me to run the kernel selector revert, I can push a quick job. If it reproduces, we can reroute traffic to fallback model variant.
